# Variadic Logging

The [logging demo](https://github.com/mattilaa/mlang/blob/main/examples/variadic_logging.mla) accepts mixed argument types:

```rust
log("INFO", "connected", "client", 42, "ready", true);
log("DEBUG", "gain", 1.5);
log("INFO");
```

Output uses MLang's normal `format!` conventions (booleans are `1`/`0` and
floating-point values have six decimal places):

```text
[INFO] connected client 42 ready 1
[DEBUG] gain 1.500000
[INFO]
```

The [logger](https://github.com/mattilaa/mlang/blob/main/examples/variadic_logging/logger.mla) forwards `args...` from `log` to `format_record` and
then to `collect`. The comma fold `(collect_one(&mut parts, args), ...)`
formats each argument using its concrete type and appends it to a
[`list<str8>`](Quick-Guide#types) in argument order. No C varargs or runtime type tags are involved.
Each argument must support `format!("{}", value)`.

From the repository root:

```sh
build/mlang examples/variadic_logging.mla -o /tmp/variadic_logging
/tmp/variadic_logging
build/mlang --tests examples/variadic_logging_tests.mla
build/mlang --tests tests/variadic_generic_tests.mla
```

The logging tests use the same module as the demo. They check mixed types,
exact output, empty and single-element packs, repeated specializations,
append order, and evaluation of arguments exactly once from left to right.

For nested structured output, see the [JSON logging demo](https://github.com/mattilaa/mlang/blob/main/examples/variadic_json_logging.mla).
It uses the standard-library module [`std::log::json`](https://github.com/mattilaa/mlang/blob/main/stdlib/std/log/json.mla)
and prints both compact and indented JSON. Run it and its tests with:

```sh
build/mlang examples/variadic_json_logging.mla -o /tmp/variadic_json_logging
/tmp/variadic_json_logging
build/mlang --tests tests/std_log_json_tests.mla
```
